name: How do I keep a renovation on budget when materials prices change?

mainEntity.name: What can homeowners do if finish selections or material costs rise after the project starts?
mainEntity.text: What can homeowners do if finish selections or material costs rise after the project starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Material price changes are common, especially when projects depend on custom or long-lead items. The best defense is early selection of the major budget drivers: flooring, tile, cabinetry, lighting, fixtures, and specialty millwork. Homeowners should ask the contractor which items are already locked, which are allowance-based, and which are still flexible. When prices increase, the project can often be protected by swapping to alternate finishes, simplifying custom details, or reducing nonessential scope. The key is to make those decisions quickly and in writing before the change affects scheduling. A transparent contractor should notify you as soon as a cost shift appears, not after the work is already ordered. That gives you time to keep the renovation financially under control without sacrificing the whole project.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best way to stay on budget is to lock in decisions early, use realistic allowances, and get written approval for substitutions before ordering changes. If prices rise, the contractor should show the impact immediately so you can adjust scope or finishes before the overage grows.
